verdict.rationale: A hands-on probe got HTTP 200 for a real robots.txt at trademarks.ipo.gov.uk. Its directives were specific enough to tell a keyless agent it was walled off before fetching anything else, which is exactly the before-you-fetch signal the story asks for. The story concerns publishing a usable robots.txt, not whether that file is permissive, so the restrictive policy does not reduce the verdict. Missing for 10: the actual robots.txt directives are not quoted, the gov.uk guidance host's robots.txt was not probed, and there is no first-party documentation or independent corroboration of the crawl policy.
